messages:
maya: Trying to capture the follow-up from yesterday's RFC review — proposing a lightweight handshake between control-plane and operator for budget-aware prewarming. TL;DR: keep admission simple, push budget math to control-plane, operator only needs an escrow token + expiry.
aj: +1 on pushing complexity out of the operator. can you sketch the token shape?
maya: Sketch: control-plane issues a PrewarmEscrow token (opaque string) with fields: budget_id, max_cost_units, expiry_ts, optional tags. operator uses token to allocate prewarm slots and reports back consumption.
sam: how do we prevent double-spend if control-plane retries or network flaps?
maya: operator must atomically bind token -> reservation id in its local store. token can't be re-used after bind. control-plane can query reservation status via observer API.
irina: we need to reconcile metrics for billing: operator reports prewarm_consumed_units with "prewarm_budget_id" tag so optimize/cost pipelines can join. is that feasible?
leo: yes, we can push a metric line: prewarm.kv.allocated_units{budget_id=...}. incremented on start and decremented on tear-down. gives near-realtime visibility without full ledger.
aj: what's the SLO for control-plane to revoke/adjust a token? if budget exhausted mid-prewarm, operator behavior matters.
maya: two modes: graceful-trim and immediate-revoke. control-plane should first attempt graceful-trim: reduce future admissions and not renew tokens. immediate-revoke only for fraud/compromise; operator must support a Revoke call.
sam: UI/UX: product teams want a visible estimate of prewarm cost before confirming. can control-plane provide a quote based on model, seq_len, and target concurrency?
maya: yes -> control-plane runs quick cost-estimator, returns estimated_units and recommends max_cost_units for token. token carries that limit. operator enforces it by refusing admission when consumption >= max_cost_units.
irina: edge: what if operator undercounts due to batching amortization? we need to define "consumption" unit. suggest we charge per GPU-minute multiplied by amortization factor for batching and caches.
leo: agree. define canonical unit = gpu_milli_minutes. operator emits consumed_gpu_milli_minutes and control-plane converts to cost units using the budget config. keeps exchangeable accounting.
aj: API shape idea: POST /prewarm-intent -> {model, concurrency, window_ms, budget_hint} -> returns {escrow_token, est_units, expiry}. operator: POST /reserve -> {escrow_token, node_filter?} -> returns reservation_id or 403. then PATCH /consume and DELETE /release.
maya: sounds good. also add GET /reservation/{id}/status for reconciliation.
sam: observability: add log line on reservation bind: "prewarm.bind budget_id=.. reservation_id=.. nodes=..". ops-bot can scrape and emit alerts if binds spike.
ops-bot: deploy note: we'll add a metric prewarm.bind.rate and alert if >3x baseline for >5m.
irina: test plan: simulate a burst of 200 small prewarms with mixed durations and ensure control-plane handles token expiry and that operator enforces max_cost_units.
leo: implementation risk: operator local store must be highly-available; we can back it by etcd but ensure bind latency <50ms for admission path. otherwise prewarm latency wins over benefit.
aj: question: do we let operator create ephemeral scratch caches for prewarm that are free to evict, or must prewarm use only normal KV cache (which costs more)?
maya: config toggle per-token: cache_tier: ephemeral|persistent. ephemeral means operator can reclaim earlier and lower accounting weight. control-plane pricing must reflect that.
sam: rollout plan: feature gated. stage 1: token + reserve/consume/release API, operator does naive accounting, control-plane handles budgets. stage 2: add revoke/graceful-trim and cache_tier. stage 3: cost-optimizations (amortization factors, batching heuristics).
irina: can we keep the audit trail in control-plane only to simplify compliance? operator must send consume/release events but not store long-term. control-plane stores ledger.
leo: that reduces operator state, but operator still needs ephemeral binding to prevent double-alloc. bind lifetime is short-lived and can be persisted in memory with leader lease. if operator restarts it will reconcile with control-plane via GET /reservation list.
aj: security: escrow tokens must be signed and expire. rotate signing keys periodically; operator validates signature before bind.
maya: agreed. add key-id header so operator knows which key to use.
sam: acceptance criteria: (1) operator rejects reserves without valid token; (2) consumed units reported within 1m of consumption; (3) control-plane can revoke and operator stops admitting new prewarms for that token within 30s.
irina: plus telemetry tags: budget_id, token_kid, cache_tier, model.
leo: any objections about keeping budget math out of operator? I worry about corner cases where operator must approximate cost for local admission fairness between tenants.
maya: proposal: operator may implement local heuristics but must never exceed token.max_cost_units. heuristics are best-effort; billing authoritative in control-plane.
aj: action items: maya to draft API proto + example token format; leo to prototype operator bind+local-store sketch; nirina to own telemetry schema; sam to write rollout checklist.
maya: I'll put a short RFC addendum today and ping infra for an etcd mini-provision for testing. thanks all :thumbsup:
